# gh-337/13 — Generated files regenerate instead of resolving

### Goal

A base update whose conflicts are all generated files is finished by norn with no agent: it takes the base side, runs the mapped commands and commits the merge with `Norn-Regenerated`. A branch holding only its spec folder takes the base side with no agent and no config (#126). On the light path a regenerated merge counts as clean.

### Proof

- AC1 (the regenerate key loads and validates; a malformed entry is refused with the reason): `packages/cli/test/integration/config.test.ts` › "regenerate is a team key: entries load with their source; a malformed entry is refused with the reason". Schema in `packages/schema/src/config.ts` (`RegenerateEntry`, `REGENERATE_TIMEOUT` = 2m). The resolved config carries `regenerate` only when the team file sets it, so golden cases and recorded replays are unchanged.
- AC2 (all conflicts mapped → base side, the matched commands bounded, merge with trailer, no agent, then test): `packages/cli/test/integration/regenerate.test.ts` › "every conflict mapped → merged with Norn-Regenerated by norn, no agent, then the test step" (through the tick: classify `done` with `base.regenerated`, no runner launch, a check receipt at `test`). Also `integrate.test.ts` › "every conflict mapped → base side, the matched commands run bounded…" (entry order, per-entry timeout, default 2m).
- AC3 (any unmapped conflict → resolve): `integrate.test.ts` › "a conflicting path no glob matches → conflict as today, nothing run, the merge aborted".
- AC4 (failed or timed-out command, or a path still conflicted → abort, resolve, output in the brief): `integrate.test.ts` › "a failing or timed-out command, or a path still conflicted, aborts the merge → conflict with the output"; `regenerate.test.ts` › "a failing command → resolve, with what it printed in the resolver's brief"; `packages/core/test/unit/base-sync.test.ts` › "2c: regenerating did not finish the merge…" (brief text, S2).
- AC5 (spec-folder-only branch takes the base side as a merge): `integrate.test.ts` › "a branch holding only its spec folder takes the base side of every conflict outside it, as a merge, with no mapping".
- AC6 (light path: clean only with the trailer and a remerge-diff inside the mapping): `packages/core/test/unit/update-outcome.test.ts` › "a regenerated merge is clean only with its trailer and a remerge-diff inside the regenerate mapping".
- AC7 (the git port merges keeping its conflicts): `packages/adapters/test/contract/git.ts` › "merge keeping its conflicts: takeSide resolves to a side, concludeMerge commits the merge, abortMerge drops it". The real adapter is the only GitPort; no git fake exists to run it against.
- AC8 (this repo's mapping and docs; agent verifier): `.agents/norn.config.yaml` maps `packages/schema/json/*.schema.json` → `bun run schema:emit` and `docs/reference.md` → `bun run docs:emit`, and no golden case. The key is documented in `docs/reference.md` › Config (fast and deterministic, default timeout, an example), in `docs/recipes.md` › The base moved under a story, and in the starter `packages/cli/assets/config.yaml`.
- `bun run test` and `bun run typecheck` are green. `schema:emit`, `docs:emit` and the `.agents/norn.config.schema.json` copy are regenerated.

### Easy to miss

- `abortMerge` is `reset --hard HEAD` + `clean -fd`, not `merge --abort`: `merge --abort` refuses once a command has rewritten a staged path. This is safe only because `update` refuses a dirty worktree before it merges.
- Every update now merges with `keepConflicts` and aborts through `abortMerge`, so the git argv of a plain conflict changed. `test/e2e/transcripts/base-sync.txt` was rewritten with `NORN_TRANSCRIPT_UPDATE=1` as the intended change. The rewrite also picked up `rev-parse refs/heads/<branch>^{commit}` lines that earlier slices' observe changes had left unpinned.
- Spec-folder-only means every non-merge commit on the first-parent line since the base touches only the spec folder, and every merge is a norn base update (`Norn-Tick` trailer and an `Update <story> from` subject). A merge of the remote branch could carry a person's work, so it disqualifies the branch. Any conflict inside the spec folder goes to resolve.
- The light path's clean check needs the trailer and every remerge-diff path matched by the current mapping. Without a mapping, nothing counts as regenerated.

### Not proven yet

- AC8 is for the agent verifier to read. No test runs `bun run schema:emit` as a regenerate command in a fresh worktree. A worktree without `node_modules` would make the command fail, and the update then goes to resolve with the output: safe, but no faster.

### Notes

- The glob matcher lives in core (`packages/core/src/regenerate.ts`, `Bun.Glob`), so act and the light path read the same mapping. Core already uses `Bun.CryptoHasher`, and the purity lint allows it.
- The classify receipt's `base` gained `regenerated` (paths taken from the base, also on a spec-folder-only merge) and `regenerate.output` (on a conflict). The receipt detail names which of the two happened.
- A config error for a missing required field now names the field (`` `regenerate.0.run` is required ``) instead of the list.
- Friction: none.

### Resume

Implementation is complete and committed. Next is the slice's test check, then review.
